summary: The independent reviewer confirmed both prior security fixes, but found three implementation gaps and one evidence gap: inbound messages lack a document token, redirect requests never set isRedirect, session destruction does not invalidate retained views, and several native lifecycle/capability paths lack durable integration evidence.

gaps.title: Bind inbound bridge messages to a document token
gaps.why_it_matters: A queued message from an old document can pass after a same-origin navigation commits because origin checks alone do not identify the sending document.
gaps.suggested_followup_issue: Issue a new document token before each main-frame navigation, require it on inbound messages, and test a stale same-origin token.

gaps.title: Populate redirect context for navigation policy
gaps.why_it_matters: Every NavigationRequest currently reports isRedirect=false, so portable policy cannot distinguish redirects.
gaps.suggested_followup_issue: Track active provisional navigation state, set isRedirect for subsequent non-user main-frame requests, and verify it with the loopback redirect.

gaps.title: Invalidate session-created views on session destruction
gaps.why_it_matters: Retained views own the policy independently and can continue callbacks after their session is destroyed.
gaps.suggested_followup_issue: Register views with shared session state, close all registered views when the session dies, and test a retained view.

gaps.title: Retain complete macOS integration evidence
gaps.why_it_matters: Stop, reload, permitted popup inheritance, native capability callbacks, and callback races lack matching durable integration evidence.
gaps.suggested_followup_issue: Add the missing real WKWebView scenarios and commit a final clean test report with the mission artifacts.

assumptions: profilePath remains a logical macOS profile identifier.
Only macOS is implemented in this mission.

outcome_answers.answer: Yes. Public creation is session-only, and the former standalone factory plus unrestricted page bridge/popup APIs are absent from public C++, demo, tests, and documentation.
outcome_answers.boundary: This is intentionally source-breaking; no compatibility shim is provided.

outcome_answers.answer: Yes. Configurations from one macOS session share its website data store and process pool, receive distinct content controllers, and ephemeral sessions use a non-persistent store.
outcome_answers.boundary: profilePath is logical on macOS; arbitrary storage placement and stronger process isolation are not promised.

outcome_answers.answer: Lifecycle IDs, failures, policy rejection, popup rejection, outbound generation checks, and idempotent close exist, but redirect policy context and session-bound callback lifetime are incomplete.
outcome_answers.boundary: Allowed popup inheritance, stop/reload, native capability callbacks, and overlapping callback races need stronger integration evidence.

outcome_answers.answer: Origin, main-frame, envelope, size/version/type/schema, outbound argument binding, and hostile-payload behavior are enforced, but inbound same-origin stale documents are not tied to the active document token.
outcome_answers.boundary: The hostile test proves outbound data-only delivery, not stale inbound document rejection.
outcome_answers.next_action: Complete FOLLOWUP-03 and add the same-origin stale-token test.

outcome_answers.answer: At design-contract level, yes. Public headers expose portable Qt/C++ types and documentation maps the concepts to WKWebView, WebView2, and WebKit2GTK without native profile types.
outcome_answers.boundary: Only macOS is implemented or production-tested.
outcome_answers.next_action: Validate each future backend when implemented.
